newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu calls on Palestinians to keep faith.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu calls on Palestinians to keep faith.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appealed to Palestinians not to lose hope in peace talks, while an Israeli official said Jews and Arabs needed a few months to cool off after an explosion of violence.
The West Bank and Gaza Strip were largely quiet on Thursday after a Washington peace summit, but many voiced doubts the calm would continue.

"I ask you, don't go into mourning. Don't lose hope," Netanyahu said on Israel Channel One television's Arabic service in an address to Palestinians. "This is an opportunity for a fresh start for the peace process."

A senior Israel official who returned with Netanyahu on Thursday from the White House summit, hailed by Israelis as a success, said a stabilisation period of some 90 days was needed after fierce clashes that killed 73 last week.
"So the two military structures can gain confidence to work together," said the official, who declined to be identifiend.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said the future of the Middle East peace process depended on Israeli moves.

"It depends how the Israelis will deal. Especially we are insisting they implement accurately and honestly what has been agreed upon and what was signed," he said before leaving for Tunis after talks with Moroccan King Hassan.
Netanyahu said Israel and the Palestinians were still far from a solution to their problems, but progress could be achieved in accelerated negotiations starting on Sunday.
"If we fight each other and if we return to bloody riots, we will both be losers. If we walk together on the process of peace...we will both be winners," Netanyahu said.

Palestinians branded the summit a failure after Arafat failed to win a target date for a long-delayed Israeli troop pullback in the West Bank town of Hebron or an Israeli pledge to close a Jerusalem tunnel under an Islamic holy site whose opening last week sparked the clashes.
"I think the violence may resume because the summit failed to wipe out the causes of the explosion," said Ayman Hassan, a Palestinian policeman in Gaza.
Netanyahu telephoned President Hosni Mubarak on Thursday to say he was sorry the Egyptian leader had not attended the Washington summit, a spokesman said.

The Israeli leader said the new round of U.S.-brokered talks, to be held on the Israel-Gaza border on Sunday, would focus on security issues and the Israeli pullout from Hebron, agreed by the previous government.
Netanyahu said he intended to honour the Hebron deal "with proper security arrangements, of course". Palestinians have rejected any renegotiation of the plan.
The Islamic Resistance Movement Hamas urged Palestinians to "total confrontation" with Israeli forces and settlers after Friday prayers in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
"The only thing that can solve this problem is a new intifada (uprising), hot confrontation against Israel," Hamas spokesman Mahmoud Zahhar told Israel television in Gaza.
Their barrels pointing from hilltops, Israeli tanks remained in positions overlooking Palestinian towns.
In Hebron, where Israeli gunfire killed an 11-year-old Arab boy on Wednesday, some 3,000 Palestinians demonstrated, burning pictures of Netanyahu and U.S. and Israeli flags.
